Class HttpClient

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.jdk.net.http.HttpClient
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class HttpClient extends Object implements AutoCloseable
The board-side java.net.http.HttpClient: sends a HttpRequest through the board's own NativeHttpRequests. See the package description for the subset.

What a program never uses is not linked: the request code of a scheme none of its URIs name, the redirect code when it never calls followRedirects, and a full response-header buffer when it never reads headers() or follows redirects.

As in the JDK since 21, a client is AutoCloseable, so it can be the resource of a try-with-resources statement. Every request runs to completion in the thread that sends it, so a client that is shut down has no request left to wait for: isTerminated() is true at once, and a later send(HttpRequest, HttpResponse.BodyHandler) throws IOException.

    • send

      public <T> HttpResponse<T> send(HttpRequest request, HttpResponse.BodyHandler<T> responseBodyHandler) throws IOException, InterruptedException
      Sends request and waits for the reply, following redirects as the client's policy says. With HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofByteArray() the response is the client's own object, refilled by every call, so read it before the next request; with HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString() it is a new object holding its own String. Either way its headers are read from the client's buffer, refilled by every call.
      Throws:
      HttpTimeoutException - when no response arrived within the timeout
      IOException - when the client is shut down, the request could not be sent, or a redirect could not be followed
      InterruptedException - never on the board; declared because the JDK method declares it

    • shutdown

      public void shutdown()
      Shuts the client down: a later send(HttpRequest, HttpResponse.BodyHandler) throws IOException. Shutting it down again does nothing.
